propositions.text: The claimants are siblings from a village in India claiming refugee protection under the Act.
propositions.quote: The claimants, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX are brothers and sisters and are from the village of XXXX in XXXX, India. They claim refugee protection pursuant to ss. 96 and 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (the "Act").1

paragraphs.summary: The claimants are siblings from India claiming refugee protection under the Act, as stated by the court.

propositions.text: The panel must find if there is a serious possibility of persecution or risk of torture, death, or cruel treatment if claimants return to India, with no protection or safe place available.
propositions.quote: The duty of this panel is to find if there is sufficient credible or trustworthy evidence to determine that there is a "serious possibility"2 that the claimants would be persecuted, or that there are substantial grounds to believe that they would be tortured, or at risk of losing their lives or being subjected to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment if they returned to India. This also means that it must not be possible to get protection from this persecution or risk from Indian authorities and, further, that there is no other place within India where they could live safely, and that it would be reasonable to do so, in the claimants' circumstances.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the panel's duty to find serious possibility of persecution or risk if claimants return to India, with no protection or safe place.

propositions.text: The decision considers testimony, evidence, and submissions, including gender guidelines for the sister.
propositions.quote: In coming to my decision, I have considered the testimony, the evidence and the written submissions by the claimants' counsel. With respect to the sister, I have also kept in mind the points raised in the Chairperson's Gender Guidelines or other Guidelines.3

paragraphs.summary: The court considered testimony, evidence, submissions, and gender guidelines for the sister in making its decision.

propositions.text: The panel decided neither claimant is a Convention Refugee or person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: The panel has decided that the neither claimant is a Convention Refugee or a person in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes neither claimant qualifies as a Convention Refugee or person in need of protection.

propositions.text: The claimants' full allegations are in their Personal Information Forms; the female claimant alleges sexual assaults by the village head from 2010 to 2011.
propositions.quote: The claimants' complete allegations are set out in answer to Question 31 of their respective Personal Information Form (PIF) and need not be repeated here in here. To summarize, the female claimant alleges that from XXXX 2010 until XXXX 2011, she worked as XXXX XXXX at the house of the village head ("Sarpanch"). After a couple of weeks of working there, on an evening when the Sarpanch's wife and children were way, the Sarpanch sexually assaulted her. Because of fear and financial needs, the female claimant continued to work there, and she was sexually assaulted on another three or four occasions.

paragraphs.summary: The court summarizes the female claimant's allegations of sexual assault by the village head from 2010 to 2011.

propositions.text: The male claimant was falsely accused of assault by the Sarpanch's daughter, detained, and later freed with his sister's help.
propositions.quote: In the third week of XXXX 2011, the female claimant's brother, i.e., the male claimant, brought lunch for his sister at Sarpanch's home. The Sarpanch's daughter was the only person at home and made sexual advances towards him. When he refused, she partially tore off her clothes, made noise and ran out of the home, pretending she was being sexually assaulted by the male claimant. The neighbours chased after the male claimant, assaulted him, took him to the Sarpanch's home and confined him to a safe place until the Sarpanch arrived. When the Sarpanch arrived, he continued to lock him up without food and water. Finally, with the help of his sister, the male claimant was freed and escaped to his friend's home until shortly before he left for Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The court recounts the male claimant's false assault accusation, detention, and escape with his sister's help.

propositions.text: The Sarpanch and others raped the female claimant to punish her for freeing her brother and threatened to kill her if she told anyone.
propositions.quote: The Sarpanch became very angry when he learnt of the female claimant's role in freeing her brother. To punish her, the Sarpanch, the neighbours who had detained the brother and a friend who had arrived with the police jeep, all raped the female claimant. They also threatened to kill her if she told anyone about what had happened.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the female claimant was raped by the Sarpanch and others as punishment and threatened with death if she told anyone.

propositions.text: The claimants allege the Sarpanch and others want to find and harm them, believing he can act with impunity due to power and connections.
propositions.quote: Both claimants allege that the Sarpanch and in the case of the female claimant, the other men who had raped her, want to find them and hurt them. They allege that because of the Sarpanch's money, connection and power, he can do this with impunity.

paragraphs.summary: The court reports the claimants' allegation that the Sarpanch seeks to harm them and can do so with impunity due to his power.

propositions.text: The female claimant is pregnant from a relationship in Canada and fears persecution as an unwed Muslim mother in India.
propositions.quote: Since the claimants have been in Canada, the female claimant has been in a relationship with a man. She is pregnant and is expecting to give birth on or about XXXX XXXX, 2012. The female claimant also alleges that as an unwed Muslim mother, she will face a reasonable possibility of persecution at the hands of the society at large.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the female claimant's pregnancy and her fear of persecution as an unwed Muslim mother in India.

propositions.text: The claimants have established their identity and nationality as Indian citizens and are siblings with the same last name.
propositions.quote: The claimants' original passports and other identity documents were seized by Citizenship and Immigration Canada, copies of which are in Exhibit 2. I find that the claimants have established their identity and nationality as citizens of India. They also have the same last name. I accept that they are brother and sister.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimants have established their Indian identity and sibling relationship.

propositions.text: The key issue is credibility, with a presumption of truth unless reason to doubt, and reliance on rationality and common sense.
propositions.quote: In the claimants' case, the most determinative issue is credibility. When I assess credibility, there are two principles that I follow: Firstly, when a claimant swears to the truthfulness of certain facts, this creates the presumption that what he or she is saying is true unless there is reason to doubt it.4 Secondly, when assessing credibility the panel is entitled to rely on its rationality and common sense.5In this case I find that there is reason to doubt the claimants' truthfulness for the reasons on which I will elaborate.

paragraphs.summary: The court identifies credibility as the key issue, presuming truth unless reason to doubt, and relying on rationality and common sense.

propositions.text: The female claimant met her boyfriend in 2009 in the village but their relationship started in Canada after she called him from India.
propositions.quote: The female claimant alleges that she met her current boyfriend, XXXX, in 2009 in the village. She testified that she met him while walking on the street. XXXX told her that he was going to Canada and provided her with his coordinates. The female claimant testified that she and XXXX did not start a friendship or an acquaintance then, and that their friendship and later relationship started and grew in Canada. The female claimant testified that she called XXXX when she was still in India and had obtained her Canadian visa, and told XXXX that she was traveling to Canada. It was XXXX who went to the airport and picked her up.

paragraphs.summary: The court recounts the female claimant's testimony about meeting her boyfriend in 2009 but starting their relationship in Canada.

propositions.text: The female claimant alleges one assailant in India was the brother of her boyfriend, linking assaults in India and Canada.
propositions.quote: The female claimant also alleges that during the events of XXXX 2011, one of the men who sexually assaulted her was a man by the name of XXXX, who was XXXX's brother. The female claimant provided this evidence in the context of establishing that an assault she suffered in Canada by XXXX's sons6 was related to her ordeal in India.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the female claimant's allegation that an assailant in India was her boyfriend's brother, linking assaults in India and Canada.

propositions.text: The female claimant's explanation for calling XXXX after being raped is unreasonable and lacks credibility and common sense.
propositions.quote: The female claimant was asked why she was interested to call XXXX shortly after she was raped under horribly intimidating circumstances by his brother, particularly when she did not know XXXX well at the time. She testified that he when she had talked to XXXX, she thought he would be a good man and that he would not be partial. In light of the fact that the female claimant had earlier testified she had not formed a friendship with XXXX in India, I find the claimant's answer to be unreasonable and to lack credibility and common sense.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the female claimant's explanation for calling XXXX after her rape unreasonable and not credible.

propositions.text: The female claimant's belief that assaults in Canada were related to India events is not reasonable or credible.
propositions.quote: The female claimant also testified that XXXX is still married to another woman, but that he had separated from her before the claimant arrived in Canada. The claimant and XXXX first started a friendship, and after they were attacked by XXXX's relatives, they moved in together and started a romantic relationship. They now expect to have a baby together. The claimant testified that she believed she was attacked in Vancouver on the order of XXXX's brother, XXXX, and the Sarpanch, in continuation of what had happened in India. She stated, and it is marked on the police report, that XXXX's wife, XXXX's daughter, and his two nephews, assaulted the claimant.7 The claimant was asked what made her think the assault was related to the events in India and not because XXXX's wife was angry enough at her husband's friendship/relationship with her to have mobilized the assault. The claimant stated she knew the two assaults were related because XXXX's and the Sarpanch's children are in Canada, and that XXXX's sons, who were also XXXX's nephews, were involved in the attack. I do not find the claimant's answer to be reasonable or credible.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the female claimant's belief that Canadian assaults were related to India events unreasonable and not credible.

propositions.text: The female claimant's failure to inform police about the India-related assault suspicion is not reasonable or credible.
propositions.quote: I note that the claimant never informed the police in her statement that she suspected the assault to have been related to a previous criminal act against her in India. When asked why, the claimant stated the police had never asked her the question. The police could not have been reasonably expected to have known the detailed background and relationship between the parties back in India. I therefore do not find the claimant's answer to be reasonable or credible.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the female claimant's failure to inform police about India-related assault suspicion unreasonable and not credible.

propositions.text: The female claimant's four-month delay in making a refugee claim is not reasonable given her Canadian connection and fear for life.
propositions.quote: Finally, the claimant testified that she came to Canada because she was afraid for her life in India. She was then asked why she did not make a refugee claim until approximately four months after her arrival in Canada. The claimant stated she did not know about refugee claims in Canada. I do not find her answer to be reasonable. The claimant had contacted XXXX, who lived in Canada, from India. She said that she left India because she was afraid for her life. One would reasonably expect that with her Canadian connection, she would at least attempt to learn about her options in Canada in less than a four month period. I find that the delay to be consistent with the claimant's lack of credibility and subjective fear.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the female claimant's four-month delay in claiming refugee status unreasonable and consistent with lack of credibility.

propositions.text: The female claimant was evasive, inconsistent, exaggerated, and detached in testimony, and did not disclose rapes to doctors.
propositions.quote: I note that during the hearing, if the female claimant was asked a direct question on her PIF narrative, she would provide a consistent answer. However, when she was asked a question about the surrounding circumstances or events, she became evasive and provided long and unclear answers that required multiple repetitions. Her answers were also prone to exaggerations. For example, she stated that she believed the Sarpanch and the others would immediately kill her upon finding her. I also note that the claimant's detached demeanour was also inconsistent with what is reasonably expected of someone of the claimant's profile who had lived through her alleged experiences. More importantly, she stated that she never told a doctor about her multiple rapes, even in Canada when she has access to medical care, and in fact, she receives it as part of her pre-natal care.8 In short, I do not have sufficient credible evidence that the claimant experienced what she alleges happened in India.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the female claimant evasive, inconsistent, exaggerated, detached, and lacking credible evidence of alleged rapes.

propositions.text: The female claimant's failure to consider marriage with XXXX despite religious permissibility is inconsistent with a well-founded fear of persecution as an unwed mother.
propositions.quote: The issue now becomes whether the female claimant will face a reasonable possibility of persecution in India because of the fact that she will have a child with XXXX and that she was not married to him. The panel asked whether she and XXXX had discussed whether he would return with her to India, if she was forced to do so. She said that they had never discussed it. The claimant testified that XXXX was also a Muslim, and that under Muslim religious laws, he could get married to up to four wives. The panel asked whether she and XXXX had considered marriage as an option. She stated that they had not discussed it because in Canada, there was no need to do it. While the panel does not expect the claimant to have found becoming a second wife as a respectable or viable option, the panel was surprised that the claimant did not express any objection in principle to being a second wife. The claimant alleges that she would face persecution at the hands of individuals in India who would not approve of her not being married. In light of this, I find the fact that the claimant had not even thought of marriage, and had therefore never discussed it with XXXX, when she testified marriage would be religiously permissible and not objectionable to her, to be inconsistent with a well founded fear of persecution.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the female claimant's failure to consider marriage inconsistent with a well-founded fear of persecution as an unwed mother.

propositions.text: The female claimant's lack of knowledge about XXXX's divorce and failure to have him testify undermines her claim of fear as a single mother in India.
propositions.quote: The female claimant also testified that she did not know whether XXXX and his first wife were in the process of divorce. Given that her own fear of persecution is in part linked to being perceived to be a single mother, I find her lack of diligence in even learning about his potential divorce to be inconsistent with her allegations of fear. XXXX is also from India. The onus is on the claimant to demonstrate that she would face a reasonable possibility of persecution as a single mother in India. Yet, she never even asked XXXX to testify at the hearing to cast some light in what she did not know. Given the limited communication between the claimant and XXXX about their future together in India, I do not have sufficient credible evidence that the claimant would likely return to India as a single woman/mother.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the female claimant's lack of knowledge about divorce and failure to have XXXX testify undermines her fear claim as a single mother.

propositions.text: Elements to establish s. 97(1) claim differ from those for Convention refugee under s. 96
propositions.quote: elements necessary to establish a claim under s. 97 (1) are not identical to those necessary to establish whether a person is a Convention refugee under s. 96 of the Act.

propositions.text: Negative credibility under s. 96 not necessarily determinative under s. 97(1)
propositions.quote: a "... negative credibility determination, which may be determinative of a refugee claim under s. 96 of the Act, is not necessarily determinative of a claim under subsection 97 (1) of the Act."

propositions.text: No sufficient credible evidence to establish personal risk under s. 97(1) for claimant
propositions.quote: I do not have sufficient credible evidence that would provide a foundation for establishing a personal "risk" for the claimant pursuant to s. 97 (1) of the Act.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains s. 97(1) claims differ from s. 96, cites Bouaouni on credibility, and finds no credible evidence of personal risk under s. 97(1).

propositions.text: Female claimant testified Sarpanch and wife were financially generous, providing a buffalo to her family
propositions.quote: The female claimant had testified that the Sarpanch and his wife were financially generous with her... the Sarpanch provided the family with a buffalo

propositions.text: Female claimant's family had limited means; brother brought her food from home despite living with Sarpanch family
propositions.quote: her own family's financial means were very limited... her brother would bring her food from home when she lived at the Sarpanch's

propositions.text: Claimants gave evasive and vague responses about female claimant's meals; court finds them not credible
propositions.quote: I do not find the claimants' evasive and vague responses to be credible.

propositions.text: No credible evidence female claimant sometimes ate lunch from home and brother took it to her
propositions.quote: I do not have sufficient credible evidence that the female claimant would sometimes eat lunch from her family home and that the brother would then take it to her.

paragraphs.summary: The female claimant testified about financial help and meals; the court finds their responses evasive and not credible regarding lunch arrangements.

propositions.text: Male claimant alleges Sarpanch's daughter made sexual advances and falsely accused him of assault
propositions.quote: The male claimant alleges that... the Sarpanch's older daughter opened the door and made sexual advances towards him... she pretended that the male claimant had attempted to sexually assault her.

propositions.text: Male claimant gave vague, evasive answers about sexual behaviour stigma and power dynamics in village
propositions.quote: The male claimant's answer to these points was very vague and evasive.

propositions.text: Court finds male claimant evasive and lacking credibility
propositions.quote: I find the claimant to have been evasive and to lack credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The male claimant alleges false sexual assault accusation; court finds his answers vague, evasive, and not credible.

propositions.text: Male claimant said no formal charges due to Sarpanch family's desire to keep matter private
propositions.quote: He stated that there were not because the Sarpanch family did not want to make it public

propositions.text: Male claimant later said everyone in village thought he tried to rape Sarpanch's daughter
propositions.quote: he later testified that everybody in the village thought that he had tried to rape the Sarpanch's daughter.

propositions.text: Court finds claimant's answers lack credibility and infers no objective documentary evidence of charges
propositions.quote: I find the claimant's answer to lack credibility. I would therefore make an adverse inference that there is no objective documentary evidence, such as evidence that the claimant has been charged.

paragraphs.summary: The male claimant's contradictory statements about charges lack credibility; court infers no documentary evidence of charges exists.

propositions.text: Even accepting male claimant's allegations, he has a viable internal flight alternative (IFA) in other cities
propositions.quote: Even if I accept the male claimant's allegations, I still find that he has a viable internal flight alternative (IFA) outside of his village in cities such as Ganhinagar, Jaipur or Delhi.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds male claimant has a viable internal flight alternative in other cities even if allegations are accepted.

propositions.text: To find viable IFA, panel must be satisfied no serious persecution risk and it is reasonable to seek refuge there
propositions.quote: the panel must be satisfied that (1) there is no serious possibility of the claimant being persecuted... and (2) that conditions... would be reasonable... for him to seek refuge there.

paragraphs.summary: Court states legal test for viable internal flight alternative requires no serious risk and reasonableness to seek refuge there.

propositions.text: In Rasaratnam, burden on claimant to show no viable IFA is high, requiring concrete evidence of adverse conditions
propositions.quote: once IFA is raised as an issue, the onus is on the claimant to show that he or she does not have an IFA... requires nothing less than the existence of conditions that would jeopardize the life and safety of the claimant

paragraphs.summary: Court cites Rasaratnam that claimant bears high burden to prove internal flight alternative is unreasonable with concrete evidence.

propositions.text: Claimants testified village has about XXXX inhabitants
propositions.quote: The claimants testified that their village has approximately XXXX XXXX XXXX inhabitants.

propositions.text: Claimants said Sarpanch could find them anywhere in India due to money and power
propositions.quote: The claimants testified that with money and power, everything was possible in India.

propositions.text: Male claimant escaped to friend's village and Sarpanch did not find him
propositions.quote: the male claimant allegedly escaped from the Sarpanch home to a friend's home in another village in XXXX, stayed there for a few weeks until he came to Canada, and the Sarpanch still did not find him.

propositions.text: Female claimant alleged one rapist was a XXXX XXXX; court did not find her credible
propositions.quote: The female claimant had testified that one of her rapists was a XXXX XXXX. For reasons I have explained, I have not found her to be credible.

propositions.text: Even if accepted, Sarpanch's connections would not likely help him find claimants outside XXXX
propositions.quote: this would not credibly establish that the Sarpanch connections to a XXXX XXXX XXXX in XXXX would reasonably get him very far with information outside of XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: Claimants testified about village size and Sarpanch's power; court finds escape and lack of credible evidence limit Sarpanch's reach outside village.

propositions.text: Male claimant not charged and not wanted criminal; unlikely to face arrest in cities like Delhi
propositions.quote: the claimant is not a wanted man as a criminal, and as such, he will not face a risk of arrest by officials in cities such as Ganhinagar, Jaipur or Delhi.

propositions.text: No central registry in India; some states have registries but no evidence Sarpanch can monitor
propositions.quote: a central registry does not exist in India... I do not have sufficient credible evidence that the Sarpanch has the means of monitoring it.

propositions.text: Japur and Delhi are outside XXXX; unlikely claimant faces persecution or harm there
propositions.quote: both Japur and Delhi are cities outside of XXXX. I find that it will be unlikely that the claimant would face a reasonable possibility of persecution, or a personal risk of harm in a city such as Delhi.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds male claimant not charged or wanted, no registry monitoring evidence, and unlikely to face harm in cities outside village.

propositions.text: Female claimant alleges Sarpanch's family in Vancouver would notify Sarpanch of claimants' return to India
propositions.quote: The female claimant alleges that... the Sarpanch's and XXXX's family members in Vancouver would notify XXXX and the Sarpanch of the claimants' return.

propositions.text: Male claimant could move away from Vancouver to avoid notification; no credible evidence Sarpanch could find him in India
propositions.quote: nothing is preventing him to move away from Vancouver... I find I do not have sufficient credible evidence that he could find the claimant in a large country of over a billion people.

paragraphs.summary: Female claimant alleges Sarpanch's family would notify Sarpanch; court finds male claimant could avoid this and no credible evidence Sarpanch could find him in India.

propositions.text: Male claimant said low education prevents living outside village; court finds this unreasonable and not credible
propositions.quote: he stated that with his low level of education, he could not live anywhere outside of his village... I do not find his assertion... to be reasonable or credible.

propositions.text: Male claimant is young, literate, has traveled to Canada, works in Canada, and communicates in English
propositions.quote: He is a young man who has travelled half way across the world to Canada... he has gone to school until grade 12... he works in XXXX and he said he could communicate with coworkers and customers in English.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds male claimant's claim of inability to live outside village unreasonable given his literacy, travel, work, and English skills.

propositions.text: Burden on claimant to show IFA unreasonable is high; claimant failed to discharge it
propositions.quote: the burden on the claimant to establish that the IFA is unreasonable is rather high. The claimant has not led sufficient credible evidence to discharge this burden.

propositions.text: Considering conditions and circumstances, it is not objectively unreasonable for claimant to seek refuge in Delhi
propositions.quote: Having considered the conditions in Delhi and all the circumstances of this case... I find that it is not objectively unreasonable for the claimant to seek refuge there.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds claimant failed to meet high burden to show IFA unreasonable and it is reasonable to seek refuge in Delhi.

propositions.text: Viable IFA is fatal to claims under ss. 96 and 97(1); male claimant's claims fail
propositions.quote: Since having a viable IFA is fatal to claims made under both ss. 96 and 97(1) of the Act, I find that the male claimant's claim under both sections fails.

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes male claimant's claims under ss. 96 and 97(1) fail due to viable internal flight alternative.

propositions.text: Claimants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection
propositions.quote: I determine that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: Court determines claimants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection.
